mono-7101.d: HELLO, WORLD spelled in eight-bit ASCII: each character's code as eight bits, ones filled and zeros open, its hexadecimal value beside it. Measured before it was drawn.

mono-7102.d: Select Graphic Rendition and screen codes of ANSI X3.64 (ECMA-48), the escape sequences terminals still obey. Computed, not invented.

mono-7103.d: The first fifteen POSIX signals with their Linux numbers and default actions, from the hangup to the polite request to terminate. Measured before it was drawn.

mono-7104.d: The HTTP status codes met most often, with their reason phrases as RFC 9110 gives them. Computed, not invented.

mono-7105.d: Unix file permissions: each octal digit the sum of read 4, write 2 and execute 1, with the two modes most files carry. Every mark stands for something real.

mono-7106.d: Box-drawing characters from the Unicode range U+2500 to U+257F: light, heavy, double and rounded lines, corners, tees and crosses. Drawn from published values.
